prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The map separates a very near dirt embankment along the bottom from the more distant field, tree line, utility poles, and sky; the person remains in front of the camera wearer and appears roughly 2–4 m away, while the trees and poles are tens of metres away. Across the five frames, the person shifts from left to right and becomes slightly larger/brighter, suggesting a modest approach or lateral pass rather than a clear retreat; in frame 5, the carried tool is similarly near and extends to the person’s right. The bright foreground indicates that the dirt at the bottom edge may be within about 1–2 m of the wearer, whereas nothing clearly enters the wearer’s arm’s reach. This map makes near–far layering and the continuous relief of the dirt easier to see than RGB, but its black sky, weak object boundaries, relative rather than metric scale, and merged person/tool depths make exact distances unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation isolates one foreground person in every frame, moving from the lower-left region toward the lower-right while staying in front of the camera wearer; the mask grows somewhat, consistent with a small decrease in distance from roughly 3–4 m to roughly 2–3 m. No other people are segmented, and the landscape, trees, poles, dirt, and the tool visible in frame 5 are not given usable masks, so their spacing and reachability cannot be determined from this map alone. The person is partly cut off by the bottom edge in all frames, and the frame-5 tool is largely absent from the mask even though it lies beside and partly overlaps the person in RGB. The map clarifies the person’s silhouette against the similarly colored ground, but the frame-1 label “bird” is plainly unreliable and the missing tool/background instances make the scene layout incomplete.
descriptions.pose: The yellow skeleton tracks a single person low in each frame, progressing from left to right and becoming somewhat larger; the changing limb geometry indicates turning from a more side-on or bent posture toward a more upright side-facing posture, followed by a bent or stepping posture in frame 5. The person generally appears oriented across the scene rather than squarely toward the camera wearer, and the sparse head keypoints do not reliably establish gaze or eye contact. Their hands remain close to their own torso or within their own arm’s reach, while neither the person nor any detected limb appears within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach; the frame-5 tool is not represented as a skeleton. Pose makes joint arrangement and posture changes clearer than RGB, but lower-body joints are repeatedly clipped by the bottom edge, several limbs collapse or disappear, and the isolated small skeleton in frame 2 is especially unreliable.
